passages.text: But I had now found the goodly pearl, which, selling all that I had, I ought to have bought, and I hesitated.
passages.note: Knowing what is right yet hesitating to commit

passages.text: The conquering commander triumpheth; yet had he not conquered unless he had fought; and the more peril there was in the battle, so much the more joy is there in the triumph. The storm tosses the sailors, threatens shipwreck; all wax pale at approaching death; sky and sea are calmed, and they are exceeding joyed, as having been exceeding afraid. A friend is sick, and his pulse threatens danger; all who long for his recovery are sick in mind with him. He is restored, though as yet he walks not with his former strength; yet there is such joy, as was not, when before he walked sound and strong.
passages.note: Joy deepened by danger and hardship survived

passages.text: Every where the greater joy is ushered in by the greater pain.
Woe is me! how high art Thou in the highest, and how deep in the deepest! and Thou never departest, and we scarcely return to Thee.
passages.note: God never leaves; we rarely return

passages.text: Up, Lord, and do; stir us up, and recall us; kindle and draw us; inflame, grow sweet unto us, let us now love, let us run.
passages.note: Prayer to be roused from apathy
